source_evidence.observation: The exercise supposes that a random variable X satisfies E exp(lambda^2 X^2) <= exp(K lambda^2) for all real lambda and some constant K, and asks to show that X is bounded, explicitly glossed as ||X||_infinity < infinity.
The proposition declares its parameters K_i positive. Property (iii) is the local assertion that there is K_3 > 0 for which E exp(lambda^2 X^2) <= exp(K_3^2 lambda^2) whenever |lambda| <= 1/K_3.

source_evidence.location: PDF pages 13 and 15; printed pages 24 and 26
source_evidence.observation: The proposition adds the centering assumption E X = 0 only for equivalence with property (v), whereas Exercise 2.5.5(b), which concerns property (iii), states no centering assumption.

The title identifies the exercise as concerning property (iii) of Proposition 2.5.2; part (a) contrasts the global premise in part (b) with the standard Gaussian square-MGF, which is finite only on a bounded neighborhood of zero.

No mean-zero, symmetry, Gaussianity, independence, or other distributional hypothesis is imposed. [E1; E3; E4]

details: The logical shape is: for a random variable X, if there exists one constant K such that the displayed estimate holds for all lambda in R, then ||X||_infinity < infinity. [E1]
K may depend on X but may not depend on lambda. [E1]
Both X and lambda are squared inside the left exponential: exp(lambda^2 X^2). [E1]
The source's exercise has exp(K lambda^2) on the right, whereas the referenced property (iii) writes exp(K_3^2 lambda^2). [E1; E2]
The estimate is required for all lambda in R, including arbitrarily large |lambda|. [E1]
Replacing this by a neighborhood-of-zero condition would recover the qualitative domain of property (iii) and would not support the exercise's boundedness conclusion. [E2; E4]
The explicit requested conclusion is only finiteness of ||X||_infinity. [E1]

Analyst inference from the displayed premise: if the premise is satisfiable, then K >= 0 and X^2 <= K almost surely; hence the premise actually yields the quantitative bound ||X||_infinity <= sqrt(K) under the standard essential-supremum reading. This sharper inequality is not stated verbatim by the exercise. [E1]
At lambda = 0 the displayed inequality is tautological; the conclusion depends on having the estimate at arbitrarily large |lambda|. [E1]
Analyst inference: no negative real K can satisfy the premise, while K = 0 forces X = 0 almost surely. The local exercise does not separately discuss these cases. [E1]
X is the single random variable whose square-MGF is controlled and whose boundedness is concluded; no auxiliary random variable is introduced. [E1]
The result does not use the centering assumption associated with property (v). [E3]

undebatable_constraints: One constant K must work uniformly for every lambda in R. [E1]
The lambda domain is all of R, not merely |lambda| <= 1/K_3 or another neighborhood of zero. [E1; E2]
The hypothesis is E[exp(lambda^2 X^2)] <= exp(K lambda^2), with exactly the displayed squares and inequality direction. [E1]
The conclusion is boundedness of X, explicitly ||X||_infinity < infinity. [E1]
No centering assumption E X = 0 belongs to this exercise. [E1; E3]
The exercise asks for the implication from the global square-MGF bound to boundedness; it does not state an equivalence or a converse. [E1]
The same X occurs in the expectation hypothesis and in the L-infinity conclusion. [E1]

ambiguities.issue: The exercise says 'some constant K' without explicitly writing K > 0 or specifying K's number domain.
ambiguities.evidence: Exercise 2.5.5(b) omits a sign annotation for K [E1], while Proposition 2.5.2 declares the analogous parameters K_i > 0 [E2].
ambiguities.impact: The inherited intended reading is a positive real constant. Logically, allowing an arbitrary real K does not add nonvacuous negative-K cases, because the hypothesis itself forces K >= 0; K = 0 is the degenerate X = 0 case.

ambiguities.issue: The cited local passage does not define ||X||_infinity.
ambiguities.evidence: The exercise itself identifies boundedness with ||X||_infinity < infinity but gives no local definition of that norm [E1].
ambiguities.impact: The standard probability-theory reading is the essential-supremum norm and thus almost-sure boundedness. A pointwise-for-every-outcome interpretation would be sensitive to null-set changes and should not be substituted without an explicit convention.

contract_plain_english: For a real-valued random variable X, assume there is one constant K, fixed independently of lambda, such that E[exp(lambda^2 X^2)] is at most exp(K lambda^2) for every real lambda. Then X must be bounded in the source's L-infinity sense: ||X||_infinity is finite. The essential feature is the bound for arbitrarily large |lambda|; ordinary sub-gaussian property (iii) only requires such a square-MGF estimate near zero. No mean-zero assumption is part of this claim. [E1; E2; E3; E4]
